title: Bulbs side by side
body: Here each bulb has its own path to the battery. Scientists call this a parallel circuit. Each path gets the battery's full push.
A battery works like a pump with a steady push. It doesn't hand out a fixed amount of flow. Add a new path and the pump simply sends more. The total flow is the flow down each path added together.
So each bulb side by side glows about as brightly as one bulb alone. A real battery loses a tiny bit of its push inside. So each extra bulb dims them all a little, and the battery runs down sooner.
equation: flow from the battery = flow through bulb A + flow through bulb B
realWorld: The sockets in your home are wired side by side like this. Switching on a lamp doesn't make the TV dimmer.
sources: OpenStax College Physics 2e, §21.1 Resistors in Series and Parallel. https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/21-1-resistors-in-series-and-parallel
